ar-75098002.stem: Which fibrocartilaginous ring deepens the glenohumeral joint?
ar-75098002.explanation: The glenoid cavity is shallow; the glenoid labrum around it deepens the socket. The long head of biceps attaches to its upper part; a tear there is a SLAP lesion, and a tear of the anteroinferior part a Bankart lesion.

ar-d0f60251.stem: A 50-year-old painter has pain between 60° and 120° when raising the arm sideways (painful arc). Which rotator cuff tendon is impinged under the acromion and torn most often?
ar-d0f60251.explanation: The supraspinatus tendon passes through the narrow space between the acromion, coraco-acromial ligament and humeral head. It is impinged in the mid-range of abduction (subacromial impingement); degeneration and tears are most common in this tendon, in its poorly vascularised zone.

ar-873e5e75.stem: Why does the 'carrying angle' of the elbow exist?
options: The radial head is longer than the ulna
The medial edge of the trochlea lies lower than the lateral edge
The radial collateral ligament is short
The capitulum of the humerus is large
ar-873e5e75.explanation: In extension the forearm angles outwards relative to the arm (~10° in men, ~15° in women). This is because the medial lip of the trochlea extends further down. Cubitus valgus and varus are an increase and decrease of this angle.

ar-49c6e4a8.stem: Which of the following about the elbow joint is FALSE?
options: The ulnar collateral ligament protects against valgus stress.
The humero-ulnar joint is a hinge joint.
The anular ligament encircles the radial head.
Both flexion and rotation occur at the humeroradial joint.
The proximal radio-ulnar joint has a separate joint capsule.
ar-49c6e4a8.explanation: The elbow is a compound joint of the humero-ulnar, humeroradial and proximal radio-ulnar joints, all three within a single capsule. The medial (ulnar) collateral ligament protects against valgus stress, the lateral (radial) collateral ligament against varus stress.

ar-4fb954c8.stem: At which joints do pronation and supination occur?
ar-4fb954c8.explanation: In pronation–supination the radius rotates proximally within the radial notch of the ulna and distally around the head of the ulna. The two pivot joints work together with the interosseous membrane.

ar-ffc10707.stem: Which of the following does NOT directly take part in the radiocarpal joint?
options: Distal articular surface of the radius
ar-ffc10707.explanation: The radiocarpal joint is formed proximally by the radius and the triangular fibrocartilage disc (TFCC) and distally by the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum. The ulna is separated from the carpal bones by the disc, so it does not enter the joint directly.

ar-51873285.stem: What type of joint are the metacarpophalangeal joints?
ar-51873285.explanation: MCP joints are ellipsoid: flexion–extension and abduction–adduction occur, with no active rotation. The interphalangeal joints are pure hinge joints.

ar-2a268400.stem: Which ligament, known as the strongest in the body, prevents hyperextension of the hip?
options: Ligament of the head of the femur
ar-2a268400.explanation: The inverted-Y iliofemoral ligament (Bigelow's ligament) runs between the AIIS and the intertrochanteric line. When standing it passively stops the trunk falling backwards, allowing upright posture without muscular effort.

ar-4674d825.stem: In a traffic accident a driver's knee struck the dashboard; the leg is shortened, flexed, adducted and internally rotated. A hip dislocation is found. Which nerve is most often injured in this dislocation?
ar-4674d825.explanation: In a 'dashboard' injury with the knee bent, the femoral head dislocates posteriorly (most hip dislocations). Behind, the head compresses or stretches the sciatic nerve; the fibular part is most often affected.

ar-561bb137.stem: The artery running within the ligament of the head of the femur is usually a branch of which artery?
ar-561bb137.explanation: The artery of the ligament of the head (acetabular artery) is a branch of the obturator artery; in childhood it makes an important contribution to the femoral head, in adults only a small one. In adults the head is mainly supplied by the medial circumflex femoral artery.

ar-74361042.stem: A footballer hears a 'pop' from his knee while changing direction suddenly, and the knee swells rapidly. On examination, with the knee at 90° of flexion, the tibia slides excessively forwards. Which structure is injured?
ar-74361042.explanation: The anterior cruciate ligament prevents the tibia sliding forwards on the femur; the anterior drawer and Lachman tests are positive. The posterior cruciate ligament prevents it sliding backwards (posterior drawer test).

ar-9a262b50.stem: What is the main reason the medial meniscus tears more often than the lateral meniscus?
options: It is firmly attached to the tibial collateral ligament and so is less mobile
It is attached to the popliteus tendon
It has no blood supply at all
It is fused with the posterior cruciate ligament
It is smaller and more circular
ar-9a262b50.explanation: The medial meniscus is C-shaped and its outer edge is attached to the medial collateral ligament; because it cannot move during movement, it tears. The lateral meniscus is more circular and mobile; the popliteus tendon separates it from the collateral ligament. 'Unhappy triad': MCL + ACL + medial meniscus.

ar-c86f32a6.stem: Which muscle unlocks the knee, locked in full extension, so that flexion can begin?
ar-c86f32a6.explanation: In the last degrees of full extension the femur rotates medially on the tibia and the knee locks. At the start of flexion popliteus unlocks it by rotating the femur laterally (or, when not weight-bearing, the tibia medially).

ar-dd74f351.stem: In a valgus stress caused by a blow to the outer side of the knee, which ligament is damaged first?
ar-dd74f351.explanation: A force from the outside stretches the medial side of the knee (valgus): the medial collateral ligament tears, and in severe injuries the ACL and medial meniscus are also involved. The lateral collateral ligament is injured in varus stress.

ar-b47c2724.stem: A young woman who rolled her ankle inwards on uneven ground has swelling and tenderness in front of the lateral malleolus. Which ligament is most often injured?
ar-b47c2724.explanation: Most ankle sprains occur in plantarflexion and inversion; the anterior talofibular ligament, the weakest lateral ligament, tears first, followed by the calcaneofibular ligament. The medial deltoid ligament is very strong and is usually injured together with a malleolar fracture.
